quiz.0.question: What legend is Cirò DOC associated with?
quiz.0.options.0: It was the wine offered to the gods of Olympus
quiz.0.options.1: It was supposedly the Krimisa wine drunk by athletes at the ancient Greek Olympics
quiz.0.options.2: It was favoured by Julius Caesar
quiz.0.options.3: It was the wine of the Norman kings of Sicily
quiz.0.explanation: Legend holds that Cirò (known as Krimisa in ancient Greek times) was the wine given to victorious athletes at the ancient Greek Olympics — making it one of the world's oldest wine traditions.
quiz.1.question: Why is Gaglioppo called 'the Pinot Noir of the South'?
quiz.1.options.0: It has the same DNA as Pinot Noir
quiz.1.options.1: Like Pinot Noir, it has a pale colour, high acidity and elegant rather than powerful character
quiz.1.options.2: It is grown on granite soils like Burgundy
quiz.1.options.3: It was imported from Burgundy in the 18th century
quiz.1.explanation: Gaglioppo shares Pinot Noir's paradox: it has a pale, translucent colour despite producing deeply flavoured wines with high acidity, delicate tannins and aromatic complexity.
quiz.2.question: What is the typical alcohol content of Greco di Bianco DOC?
quiz.2.explanation: Greco di Bianco is a passito sweet wine made from sun-dried Greco Bianco grapes — one of Calabria's rarest wines with typically 17%+ alcohol and intense apricot and honey flavours.
quiz.3.question: What is 'Nduja?
quiz.3.options.1: A spicy, spreadable pork salami from Spilinga, Calabria
quiz.3.explanation: 'Nduja is Calabria's most famous food product — a fiery, spreadable salami made from pork and Calabrian chilli peppers, from the town of Spilinga. It has become globally celebrated.
